parse.title: A behaviour with no test naming it fails the build

steps.text: this is stage 0's stated deliverable in docs/timeline.md

parse.title: Could-not-look is never reported as green

steps.text: exit 2 is distinct from 0 AND from 1 — a gate that reads nothing and
exits 0 is indistinguishable in CI from a passing one

parse.title: A mapping naming a test that no longer exists is a hard failure

steps.text: this checkability is the whole argument for option C over markers

parse.title: The reader refuses when its two counts disagree

steps.text: the two counts must be different MECHANISMS — position versus lexical
structure — or agreement between them proves nothing

parse.title: An unbound noun is refused, and the missing noun is named

steps.text: no locator is ever guessed from the noun's own name

parse.title: An unsupplied route param is refused rather than truncated

steps.text: emitting ./editor/ would navigate to the wrong page and look correct

parse.title: An unrecognised keyword is an error, not silently dropped

steps.text: a spec language that ignores what it does not understand is how a

parse.title: A hole in one behaviour is filled by a different behaviour

steps.text: this is the part no BDD tool has, and it needs ONE symbol table

parse.title: Two behaviours disagreeing is a conflict, with both sides named
An inference is included by default and marked unreviewed

steps.text: James's call on claude-code-bot#68 — default-include, marked

parse.title: A verb the server has no meaning for reaches no handler

steps.text: decision 2 landed on 2026-09-08, so POST now has a handler and this
behaviour narrowed rather than disappeared — PUT, PATCH and DELETE have
one meaning each that nobody has decided, and a route accepting a verb it
cannot serve is a 405 waiting to be discovered as a 500

parse.title: The server binds the loopback interface, not every interface

steps.text: 0.0.0.0 would publish every corpus in the working tree, and the absolute
path of every repo beside it, to anything that can reach the host

parse.title: A traversal in an app name is refused rather than resolved to a path

steps.text: the name is looked UP in the set of corpora that exist; it is never
joined to a path, so there is nothing to traverse with

parse.title: Coverage that could not be read is null in the list, never zero

steps.text: project.js's rule, carried through the transport — a UI that cannot tell
"no mapping exists" from "nothing is covered" renders the second

parse.title: An edit splices one block, so every comment in the corpus survives

steps.text: a round-trip through parse() would delete every comment in the file, and
snip-it.beh's nine opening lines are the caveat everything else rests on

parse.title: An edit that would not parse never reaches the disk

steps.text: the corpus is the source of truth for everything else Kit says, so a
writer that can corrupt it is worse than one that cannot write at all

parse.title: An edit that would change a neighbouring behaviour is refused

steps.text: a step landing in the next behaviour parses perfectly and is silently
wrong — the worst failure a writer can have

parse.title: The writer never touches git, and the file proves it rather than promising it

steps.text: a bot that commits to a spec repo cannot be un-added after the first
surprise, so the absence of child_process is asserted from source

parse.title: A write route is unreachable unless the server is bound to loopback

steps.text: decision 1 said local tool; combining reachable-from-the-network with
edits-files-in-the-working-tree is an unauthenticated remote write, and
it would arrive as a --host flag rather than as a decision of his

parse.title: A hostile page gets no CORS header, so it cannot write through the browser

steps.text: access-control-allow-origin: * was defensible while the server could
not write; with a write route it means any page the developer has open
